questions.prompt: How did Aiden and Betty use the three card colours while sorting?
choices: Red meant sell, blue meant keep, and yellow meant maybe.
Red meant keep, blue meant maybe, and yellow meant sell.
Red meant maybe, blue meant sell, and yellow meant keep.
questions.answer: Red meant sell, blue meant keep, and yellow meant maybe.
questions.evidenceText: They spent Friday evening sorting everything into three piles. A red card meant sell. A blue card meant keep. A yellow card meant maybe. By nine o'clock, the maybe pile had disappeared.

questions.prompt: Why did Aiden say the teddies would get good homes?
choices: Betty told him to advertise them.
questions.rationale: The passage says Aiden spoke mostly to himself as a form of reassurance, which shows that he was reassuring himself.
questions.evidenceText: On Saturday morning, they dragged two folding tables out to the front path and arranged everything carefully. The old teddies sat in a row at the back and looked slightly sorry for themselves. "They'll go to good homes," said Aiden, mostly to himself, as a form of reassurance.

questions.prompt: Why did Aiden keep Nelly instead of selling her?
choices: He planned to sell Nelly for more money another day.
Nelly was the most expensive toy.
Some belongings mattered more than money.
questions.answer: Some belongings mattered more than money.
questions.rationale: The evidence says Aiden held Nelly and put her inside instead of selling her for money, which shows some belongings mattered more than money.
questions.evidenceText: As Aiden folded up the last table, he found something wedged at the very back — his old stuffed elephant, Nelly, who he had completely forgotten was there. He held her for a long moment. Then he carried her inside and put her on the shelf above his desk. Some things, he decided, were not for selling.
